caption: The drawing depicts a single object, which appears to be a handheld tool constructed from wood. The tool is shown in a horizontal orientation, with a smooth, elongated handle extending from the right side of the image to the left. The handle has visible wood grain patterns in shades of light and medium brown. Attached to the left end of the handle is a curved loop structure, which tapers and flows back toward the handle, forming an open space. There is a metal fastener, likely a rivet or pin, visible near the junction where the loop meets the handle, indicating a point of articulation or attachment. The background of the drawing is off-white or light beige with slight discolorations and faint stains, and there is a signature in the lower right corner in reddish-brown ink that reads "Marius N. Hansen." The composition centers the object with ample empty space surrounding it.
title: Bootjack
